_comment: Model-tier matrix for delegation-loop review calls. Row = task category, each tier is an ordered list of {model, effort} fallbacks. See issue #179 for the research behind these picks and #182 for the schema.

coding.note: AA's Coding Agent Index number for "qwen3.8-flash-next" (73.1) was cited to justify bmo's tier0 placement here. CORRECTION (2026-10-03): the AA score above is for "qwen3.8-flash-next" by name, but bmo's live /v1/models endpoint actually serves "swift-1.5-iq3_xxs" -- a heavily-quantized (iq3_xxs) fine-tune of Qwen, a different artifact AA never scored. The AA number does not verify the real served model's quality. Treat bmo's tier0 placement here as unverified until something benchmarks swift-1.5-iq3_xxs directly on a real task, not qwen3.8-flash-next's published score.

frontend-ui.source: manual (mirrors ship/SKILL.md step 8 screenshot rule and delegation-loop/SKILL.md's visible-change effort floor)
frontend-ui.note: no tier0: UI review always escalates to tier2 on any user-visible change; there is no free-tier lane for this category

translation.source: Alconost Translation Quality Index + Linguist Evaluation (2025-2026 sample, alconost.com/en/blog/best-llm-for-translation-2026)
translation.note: Alconost's full ranking: Gemini (AQI 77.7, LE 67.8) > Claude (75.6, 58.9) > GPT (73.1, 57.6) > DeepSeek (71.5, 51.4) > DeepL. Gemini and GPT score higher than Claude but have no provider config in this repo (confirmed in #179 research), so Claude is the best model this repo can actually route to for tier1/2. DeepSeek is tier0 only because it is the one free/local model family Alconost's table actually measured -- it is 4th of 5, not a strong score, and Qwen/bmo was not tested at all. A single disagreeing data point: Alconost's separate subtitle-specific benchmark (same source, April 2026) found TranslateGemma and Gemini Flash Lite beating full Claude Sonnet on subtitle text specifically -- this tier is based on the general-purpose table, not the subtitle one. Still worth the periodic manual spot-check before trusting any of this on a real task.

prose.source: LMArena Creative Writing leaderboard (BenchLeader snapshot, 2026-09-29) and EQ-Bench Creative Writing (Sept 2026) -- the two agree on a leader, unlike the translation sources
prose.note: Claude Opus leads both leaderboards by different methodology: LMArena puts Opus 5.5 at 1521 Elo (#1) with Fable 5 close second at 1501; EQ-Bench puts Opus 5 at 2121 Elo (#1) with Kimi K3 second at 2071, GPT-5.6 Sol third. No tier0: neither leaderboard has ever scored bmo's actual local models (qwen3.8-flash-next, deepseek-v4-flash-0731) on creative writing, so the free tier's prose quality is a genuine unknown, not a guess being hidden here -- leave this row without a tier0 entry until someone runs a real check rather than picking one on no evidence.

cad-spatial.note: P3D-Bench tests Claude Opus 4.6, DeepSeek V4 Pro, and Qwen3.6-Plus head-to-head on parametric 3D generation -- the closest published proxies for bmo's local deepseek-v4-flash-0731/qwen3.8-flash-next. GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro score highest overall but have no provider config in this repo, so they are not a usable pick; Opus 4.6 is the best model this repo can actually route to, even though the paper places it in a second tier behind those two, not at the top. DeepSeek V4 Pro and Qwen3.6-Plus both land in the lowest general-purpose tier on this benchmark, clearly behind every hosted frontier model -- tier0 here means 'least-bad free option', not 'validated for CAD work'. DeepSeek is listed first only because the paper singles out Qwen3.6-Plus for markedly lower geometry scores on one image-to-3D table and does not call out DeepSeek the same way; that is a weak signal, not a confident ranking between the two. Still needs the periodic manual spot-check (#179 research) before trusting either on a real CAD task. The AA number does not verify the real served model's quality. Treat bmo's tier0 placement here as unverified until something benchmarks swift-1.5-iq3_xxs directly on a real task, not qwen3.8-flash-next's published score.
